cases.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?

answer.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?
answer.answer:
The client's daily report shows more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12 because it counts all attempts before any QC rollback, while our dashboard removes rolled-back attempts. The difference on Oct 12 is due to repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back.

- Client report counts attempts (labeled "doors") as submitted at end of day, before QC rollback [doc:client-reporting#daily-report]
- Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]
- The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]

args.query: why client daily report differs from dashboard door counts

sources.text: The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.

The client receives a daily report per office pulled from the canvassing app at the end of each day. It lists attempts (labeled "doors" in the client's sheet) and contacts as submitted, before any QC rollback. We do not edit a daily report after it is sent.

cases.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?

answer.question: What counts as flash knocking under our QC rules?
answer.answer:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

- Flash knocking definition: recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Flagging threshold: 10 or more consecutive knocks recorded less than 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Consequence: confirmed flash knocking is rolled back, removing the knocks from doors and contacts [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rollback timing: happens after the day's client report has been pulled, so it never changes a report that was already sent [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]

sources.text: Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

sources.text: Pace compares doors to date with the goal to date. The projection for Election Day assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the average daily doors of the last 7 days times the knocking days left. An office "will miss goal" when its projection is below its total goal; the shortfall is the goal minus the projection.

A contact is a knock with the result "canvassed", meaning the canvasser spoke with the voter. Not home, refused and inaccessible are not contacts. Contact rate is contacts divided by doors for the same period and office.
